# Action Policy Learning

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](policy-learning_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Robot Manipulation Policies and Control → Action Policy Learning

Learn policies that generate robot actions from observations. When the main contribution is skill structure, transitions or sequential composition, use Skill Learning and Composition. Record tasks such as in-hand manipulation and methods such as RL, VLA and tactile fusion as visible labels and topics, rather than competing primary categories.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.1] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-1"></a> | **EgoJEPA｜Human-video pretraining · Latent-action transfer · WAM**<br>[EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.20904v1)<br>Meng Cao, Can Zhao, Jinjie Wei et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `gripper` `egocentric-video` `human-demonstration-pretraining` `hand-motion-annotations` `jepa` `latent-action` `cross-embodiment` `wam` `joint-flow-matching` `embodiment-adapter` `real-world` | EgoJEPA learns latent actions through future-visual prediction conditioned on hand-motion differences, pretrains a WAM to jointly predict visual dynamics and latent actions from human videos, then fine-tunes it with robot demonstrations and embodiment-specific adapters to directly generate robot actions with less reliance on hand-crafted geometric retargeting.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Stage 1 still requires video-aligned human hand-motion annotations. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.2] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-2"></a> | **Coordi-π｜VLA · AE action representation · Bimanual coordination**<br>[Coordi-π: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19753v1)<br>Yiming Meng, Yanming Shao, Weijie Shen, Kunyang Lin, Jiayu Sun, Ping Luo, Yao Mu<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `action-expert` `action-representation` `interleaved-action-tokens` `hand-identity-embedding` `factorized-rope` `bimanual-coordination` `flow-matching` `real-world` | Coordi-π modifies the bimanual representation inside the π₀.₅ action expert (AE): it interleaves separate right/left arm–hand tokens, adds hand-identity embeddings and factorizes sequence-position/control-timestep encoding, making side identity and synchronization explicit before jointly generating synchronized bimanual actions.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Retains the π₀.₅ flow-matching objective and shares input/output projections across sides; the contribution targets action-token representation and attention positional encoding inside the AE. Inputs are three RGB views, an instruction and 46-D proprioception; each side has 22-D actions. A 30-step chunk uses 60 internal tokens, paired into 44-D simultaneous commands without alternating execution or extending the prediction horizon. Across five DexJoCo tasks, average rand-obj/rand-full success is 51.3%/32.3% versus 31.9%/18.3% for π₀.₅. Hardware uses Marvin Pro with two BrainCo Revo 2 hands: four tasks, 100 demonstrations and 20 evaluation trials per task, achieving 60/80 (75.0%) versus 49/80 (61.3%). Precise contact and assembly remain failure modes. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19753v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.3] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-3"></a> | **HiFun｜Hierarchical RL · Arm–hand coordination · Human-in-the-loop learning**<br>[HiFun: a Hierarchical Framework for Efficient Functional Dexterous Manipulation Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19518v1)<br>Linyi Huang, Guowei Huai, Weibin Liu, Shulong Jiang, Ping Tan, Weixuan Zhang, Hui Zhang, Jie Song<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `hierarchical-rl` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `sac` `rlpd` `arm-hand-coordination` `human-in-the-loop` `kinesthetic-teaching` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `contact-recovery` `dynamic-movement-primitives` `intervention-advantage-weighting` `real-world` | HiFun uses two RL policy layers: a lower-level policy learns finger-joint residuals around kinesthetic demonstration references to correct and restore contact; after freezing this policy, an upper-level policy initialized with DMP data and refined through human-in-the-loop RL learns end-effector motion and hand-skill activation strength for precise arm–hand manipulation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The lower level uses real-robot residual SAC to output 12 finger-joint residuals added to a kinesthetic reference, conditioned on observations and fingertip forces; the reference can rewind after contact disruption. The upper level uses RLPD/SAC to output a 6-D end-effector increment and continuous activation weight α, interpolating between a neutral hand pose and the corrected skill pose rather than exploring every finger joint. Train and freeze the lower policy before upper-policy training; both run at execution, with fixed lower-level weights but observation-dependent finger corrections. Separate critic heads guide arm alignment and activation timing; IAW weights imitation of human interventions by estimated advantage. Six functional tool-use/constrained-retrieval tasks on Franka Research 3 with Sharpa or XHand have 50 main trials each and 98.3% average success. The one-hour per-task cap covers upper-level online fine-tuning, with additional hand-skill learning, teaching, DMP data and reward-classifier preparation; pose randomization remains within the trained workspace. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19518v1) · [Project](https://hly-123.github.io/HiFun/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.4] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-4"></a> | **FACT｜WAM · Joint force–action prediction · Tactile closed-loop refinement**<br>[FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19155v1)<br>Zhi Cao, Yining Hong, Jiaolong Yang, Yejin Choi, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Huang Huang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` `human-demonstration-pretraining` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `future-force-prediction` `visual-tracks` `joint-flow-matching` `cascaded-action-refinement` `real-world` | FACT pretrains on human visual–tactile demonstrations, jointly predicts future video, visual tracks and coarse actions, then jointly denoises force and actions with fresh tactile feedback to refine unexecuted actions for contact-sensitive bimanual dexterity.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Both modules train with flow matching. Bidirectional attention couples future force and actions; tactile refreshes reuse coarse-plan memory and refine only the unexecuted suffix, without online weight updates. Outputs are end-effector pose changes and finger-joint targets; predicted force is not a control reference. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.5] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-5"></a> | **DexMimic｜RL trajectory tracking · Value-guided resets · Multi-trajectory training**<br>[DexMimic: A Generalist Dexterous Hand-Object Tracking Policy via Value-Guided Reset Allocation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19089v2)<br>Zhexi Luo, Zhixuan Xu, Rui Yang, Zeyu Xiao, Yiwen Hou, Lin Shao<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `reference-conditioned-policy` `hand-object-tracking` `value-guided-reset-allocation` `adaptive-initialization` `multi-trajectory-training` `bimanual` `simulation` `open-loop-replay` | DexMimic jointly learns a generalist tracking policy across human hand–object demonstrations with PPO, using its critic to allocate training resets: prioritize under-learned phases, then favor hand–object states within each phase that support continued tracking, improving multi-trajectory training efficiency.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The final reference-conditioned MLP residual policy takes recent hand–object states, object properties and future reference targets, and outputs wrist translation/rotation and finger-joint residuals added to a retargeted-reference base action. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.7] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-7"></a> | **DexCast｜HOI geometry transfer · Skeletal-temporal motion encoding · 3D diffusion policy**<br>[DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14691v2)<br>Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li, Siyao Xiao, Runqing Cheng, Xiao Lin, Zhifang Liu, Haoqian Wang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-video` `rgb-d` `video-to-robot` `hand-object-reconstruction` `hand-object-point-clouds` `demonstration-synthesis` [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `spatial-augmentation` `skeletal-topology` `temporal-motion-encoding` `variational-autoencoder` `motion-pretraining` `diffusion-policy` `sim3-equivariance` `imitation-learning` `real-world` | DexCast reconstructs and refines hand–object interactions from human RGB-D videos to generate robot demonstrations, uses hand/object point clouds in a common training/deployment format as geometric observations, and conditions a diffusion policy on pretrained skeletal-temporal motion features, enabling learning without robot teleoperation demonstrations and closed-loop execution between action chunks.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Existing HOI reconstruction and residual-RL refinement generate spatially augmented demonstrations. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.8] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-8"></a> | **AFCE｜VLA · Joint action–effect representation · Bimanual coordination**<br>[Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13212v2)<br>Min Lin, Bokai Zhou, Jianqi Lin, Kaiyuan Yang, Yicheng Chang, Junjie Yu, Xiaofan Liu, Jianhua Han, Rui Li, Shen Zhao, Xiaodan Liang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `bimanual` `bimanual-coordination` `action-representation` `action-future-coupled-effect-learning` `effect-tokens` `future-grounded-supervision` `robot-response` `visual-transitions` `state-conditioned-action-decoder` `flow-matching` `imitation-learning` `simulation` | AFCE jointly encodes demonstrated actions, realized robot motion and future visual transitions into action-decodable Effect targets, trains π₀.₅ to predict Effects from current observations, and decodes them into arm–hand commands, incorporating actions and their realized consequences into VLA policy learning.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Stage I fuses actions, realized palm/fingertip/joint changes and sparse visual transitions with three reconstruction objectives, then freezes the tokenizer and caches temporal Effect targets. Deployment uses current images, instruction and proprioception, decodes predicted Effects, executes a prefix and observes again; future-evidence encoders remain offline. Single/dual-arm configurations share an Effect backbone with separate interfaces, without established cross-hand invariance. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.10] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-10"></a> | **DextER｜Contact reasoning · Language-conditioned grasp generation · Autoregressive VLA**<br>[DextER: Language-driven Dexterous Grasp Generation with Embodied Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.16046v2)<br>Junha Lee, Eunha Park, Minsu Cho<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `contact-reasoning` `language-conditioned-grasp-generation` `autoregressive-generation` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `embodied-chain-of-thought` `contact-guided-steering` `point-cloud` `shadow-hand` `supervised-learning` `simulation` | Given an object point cloud and a language instruction, DextER first predicts which finger links contact where on the object, then conditions wrist-pose and finger-joint generation on this contact sequence within one autoregressive model; users can steer grasps by specifying partial contacts.<br>**Evaluation scope:** An MLP connects PartField point-cloud features to Qwen2.5-0.5B. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.13] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-13"></a> | **LiMA｜Asynchronous dual-system WAM · Latent diffusion bridge · Live-observation action refinement**<br>[LiMA: Bridging Long-term Imagination to Real-time Dexterous Manipulation via Asynchronous Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.28431v1)<br>Ning Chen, Yankai Fu, Junkai Zhao, Qianpu Sun, Guocai Yao, Pengwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, Shanghang Zhang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` `asynchronous-dual-system` `multi-rate-generation` `future-visual-intent` `coarse-action-prior` `latent-schrodinger-bridge` `i2sb` `spatiotemporal-adaptive-modulation` `observation-conditioned-action-refinement` `joint-video-action-generation` `diffusion-transformer` `supervised-imitation-learning` `boundary-noise-injection` `action-chunking` `long-horizon-manipulation` `cosmos-predict2` `sharpa-wave` `ur5` `real-world` | LiMA uses a slow world-action model to predict future visuals and coarse actions, initializes fast diffusion refinement from these latents, and incorporates fresh observations to generate arm–hand actions while refreshing long-horizon foresight less frequently.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Cosmos-Predict2-2B initializes the slow Dreamer: three camera views/instructions yield future visual latents and coarse actions. A scratch-trained 1B Refiner consumes these priors plus fresh vision/joint state to generate near-term action chunks and future ego-view latents. I2SB bridges intent and demonstrated execution latents; imagined visuals also modulate live features. Joint supervised training uses boundary-noise injection, without RL. Refinement is generative, not separate failure detection or additive joint residuals. The Dreamer refreshes every four Refiner updates; cached priors do not establish multi-GPU parallelism. Dual UR5s, two 22-DoF SharpaWave hands and three D435s support six tasks, each with 100 teleoperation demonstrations and 20 main evaluation trials; average success is 70.8%. H100 latency of 325 ms amortizes Dreamer overhead per 32-action chunk, 45.8% below Cosmos-Policy's 600 ms, not per-action latency. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.14] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-14"></a> | **DexTacWAM｜Visuo-tactile WAM · Multi-finger tactile compression · Contact evolution prediction**<br>[DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.24976v1)<br>Haoran Yuan, Zekai Wang, Boning Shao, Haoran Lu, Trevor Darrell, Ismini Lourentzou, Wei Zhan<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `visuo-tactile-world-model` `future-tactile-prediction` `contact-dynamics` `finger-and-pose-aware-compression` `predictive-feature-action-generation` `modality-wise-kv-normalization` `continual-vision-to-touch-learning` `flow-matching` `imitation-learning` `action-chunking` `real-world` | DexTacWAM compresses ten fingertip streams into two hand latents, jointly models visual and tactile contact evolution, and conditions an action expert on predictive visuo-tactile features to generate relative arm poses and hand actions.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A frozen visual VAE encodes each fingertip; finger identity, hand pose and temporal refinement compress five streams per hand into one latent. The action expert separately normalizes visual/tactile K/V before cross-attention. Training adapts the tactile encoder on 488 interactions, finetunes the world model on about 100 demonstrations per task, then jointly trains it and a new action expert on those demonstrations, without RL. Roughly four hours refers to recorded data, not training time. Deployment uses one world-model forward pass for predictive features, without fully rendering futures or searching trajectories. The 194-D target includes arm/hand actions, finger-force and next-proprioception predictions, not 194 joints; forces are training supervision, not deployment inputs or demonstrated direct force control. Six real-robot tasks on a dual-Sharpa-Wave platform cover occluded cube placement, handover, wiping, tongs/tomato transfer, bowl unstacking and cap unscrewing, with 20 trials per method/task.
